title: Monitoring, backup and rollback: health probes, scheduled backups, one-click rollback with an incident card
description:
Filed by architect-16a01670 from parent task-e7a3d643bde34da7b27495dbda745739 (epic breakdown, human-directed 2026-09-04; owner chose Stage 1 + Stage 2 scope).

VISION Stage 2 'monitoring, backup, and rollback' and the Operations verifier row ('deployment, telemetry, backup, rollback, incident handling - blocks at Gate 3'). Re-measured 2026-09-04: `/health/read` reports the daemon's own health only; there is no probe of a deployed product, no backup schedule, no rollback kind.

FEATURE: (a) MONITORING: for every environment with a deploy receipt, the daemon probes the health URL on a durable schedule (default 60 s, per-environment setting), records `moe-health-probe/1` {environment, sha, status, latencyMs, at} in a bounded ring (last 1440) and derives UP / DEGRADED / DOWN; three consecutive failures raise ONE Needs-you INCIDENT card 'production unhealthy since <t>: roll back to <prev sha>?' with the last error line. (b) BACKUP: scheduled backups of the project store and, per environment with a database, `pg_dump` (`<project>/.moe-next/backups/...`, sha256, retention N); every backup receipt is proven restorable by a restore-to-temp check whose sha256 is recorded. (c) ROLLBACK: `deployment.rollback {environment, toReceiptRef}` (human-only) redeploys the previous image/sha (atomic replace, same health probe) and optionally restores the database backup taken at that deploy; receipt `moe-rollback-receipt/1`. (d) UI: the Deployments card shows UP / DEGRADED / DOWN with the last probe + a latency sparkline (last hour), the backups list with restore-proof state, Rollback arm/confirm; Needs-you incident card with Roll back / Dismiss; the Health screen gains an 'Environments' section. Refusals: ROLLBACK_RECEIPT_UNKNOWN, ROLLBACK_IMAGE_MISSING, BACKUP_FAILED, PROBE_URL_MISSING.
definitionOfDone: Probe loop test with a fake target: UP -> DOWN after 3 failures raises exactly one incident card (no duplicate on continued failure) and recovery closes it; the ring is bounded at 1440; probes survive a daemon restart from durable records (no probe lost, no double schedule).
Backup test: store + pg_dump backups written on schedule; restore-to-temp sha256 equality recorded per receipt; retention prunes to N with the pruned refs listed in the receipt.

`deployment.rollback` published human-only, MCP-excluded, with the full roster backfill and bidirectional roster tests; the offline test asserts the previous image tag is redeployed and the DB restore is applied only when requested; ROLLBACK_RECEIPT_UNKNOWN, ROLLBACK_IMAGE_MISSING, BACKUP_FAILED, PROBE_URL_MISSING asserted with code + layer.
Deployments card + incident card + Health 'Environments' section against a REAL daemon (Playwright; count line quoted).

Live drive: a deployed PREVIEW environment probed for at least 10 minutes, a forced failure raises the incident card, rollback restores the previous sha - probe ring excerpt + receipts in a row comment.
Runbook + README; gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`.

comments.content:
ADVERSARIAL PASS OVER THE COMPOSED FEATURE (step 4), by seat PID 18556 / worker-60888. Read-only measurement at the integrated tree; no production byte touched. One of the four is a real gap, two are closed by construction, one is closed but untested.

(a) THE FLAPPING ENVIRONMENT — SECOND CARD: YES. HISTORY: NO. THIS IS THE GAP.
Down/recover/down opens a SECOND incident with a DIFFERENT id, and child task-6ec875f4's arm at health-probe-ring.test.ts:201 proves it BY IDENTITY, not by count. The lifecycle is sound: health-incident.ts:19 carries a PARTIAL UNIQUE INDEX `ON health_incidents(project_id, environment) WHERE closed_at IS NULL`, so at most one card per environment can be open at the database layer; :76-78 closes it on the first SUCCESS probe; :84 opens only when the last HEALTH_FAILURE_THRESHOLD probes are ALL failures. Closed rows are RETAINED (closed_at is set, the row is never deleted). So the history EXISTS and is durable.
IT IS NEVER SERVED. deployments-health-read.ts:268-270 narrows the whole list to one value — `openIncidentOf` is `incidents.findLast((incident) => incident.closedAt === null)` — and :307 puts that single value on the view as `incident`. The client mirrors it exactly: live-deployments-health.ts:71 `readonly incident: EnvironmentIncidentView | null`, singular, and the EXACT-KEY roster at :279 has no history member to decode. So an operator looking at an environment that has flapped five times today sees ONE card and no indication it is the fifth. The only trace is the numeric id printed on the card itself (incident-card.tsx:57 renders `incident ${facts.incidentId}`), which an operator would have to read as a high-water mark.
NOT COVERED. The data is one member away from being servable. Recommended as a follow-up on the epic-final hardening row (task-99f364e3), not as new production work here.

(b) ROLLBACK TO A ROLLBACK — NOT STRANDED, BUT UNTESTED AND MISLABELLED.
`deployment.rollback` does NOT write a new receipt kind. It writes a NEW `moe-deploy-receipt/1` (rollback-command.ts:103, `deployReceiptId(projectId, environment, envelope.commandId)`) through the SAME `execute(request, rollbackImage)` path the deploy uses (deploy-service.ts:346 -> :236), and deploy-ledger.ts:55 states receipts are "held in LEDGER ORDER and never collapsed". So after rolling back from B to A the ledger reads [A, B, A'], and resolveRollbackTarget's `ran[ran.length - 2]` (rollback-target.ts:40-42) resolves to B. THE OPERATOR CAN GET BACK TO B. Nobody is stranded.
Two caveats worth the operator's time. FIRST, the control is labelled "Rollback" and the thing it now does is roll FORWARD to the sha they just left — correct behaviour, confusing word, and during an incident is exactly when that costs. SECOND, IT IS UNTESTED: rollback-target.test.ts has seven arms ([A,B]->A, a trailing REFUSED, a digest-less receipt, three null cases, the 64-hex payload gate) and NOT ONE of them feeds a post-rollback history [A, B, A']. The behaviour is right by construction; the arm that would keep it right is missing.

(c) THE PROBE AND THE ROLLBACK RACING — NO FALSE INCIDENT IS REACHABLE. Two independent reasons.
When the environment is already DOWN (the case that motivates a rollback) a card is ALREADY OPEN, and health-incident.ts:74-82 returns without inserting whenever an open card exists and the latest probe is a FAILURE — the partial unique index makes a second card impossible anyway. When the environment is NOT down, a mid-switch probe would need HEALTH_FAILURE_THRESHOLD consecutive failures to raise anything, and deploy-rollback.test.ts:162 asserts the rollback "never leaves the environment with no container serving" and :134 retires the incumbent only after the candidate answered healthy — so the URL keeps answering across the switch.
The residual is cosmetic and worth stating plainly: after a successful rollback the DOWN card stays visible until the next SUCCESS probe closes it, up to one interval (60 s by default, floor 5 s). The operator can see a resolved environment still wearing its incident for up to a minute. No test drives the race directly.

(d) A BACKUP RESTORED INTO THE WRONG ENVIRONMENT — IMPOSSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION. This is the strongest of the four, and it is the one path that destroys DATA rather than availability.
applyRollbackRestore (rollback-restore.ts:178-196) derives BOTH the destination and the dump from ONE key. `readCurrentDeployReceipt(store, projectId, environment)` yields that environment's current receipt; `destination(config, environment, current.decisionId, current.sha)` resolves the database URL through the environment's OWN credential/variable resolution; `dumpToRestore(config, current.decisionId)` takes the pre-migration dump recorded on the migration receipt for THAT SAME decisionId. There is NO parameter through which a caller could name a foreign backup — the operator's payload carries only `environment`, `toReceiptRef` and `restoreDatabase` (rollback-command.ts:44-50). Crossing environments would require the daemon to resolve two different environments in one call, and only one environment string exists in the call.
Three more guards on that path: the artifact's sha256 is re-measured and compared against the value the receipt recorded, refusing DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_RESTORE_BACKUP_UNVERIFIED on any mismatch, absence, emptiness or unreadability (:154-164); boundness and dump both resolve BEFORE the single `restoreDatabaseInto` call, so every refusal happens with the database still untouched (:187-190); and it is ONE ATTEMPT, a throw is a refusal and never a retry.
